analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md, docs/reference/README.md and docs/reference/configuration.md. No executable code, workflow, protocol, key handling, attestation or cache logic changes. The edits remove retained-console wording from the test guide and reference index. They delete the "Console UI" section of NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables (base lines 82-99) from configuration.md. They reassign console and coordinator configuration to darkbloom-platform through an immutable link. They also reword the paged_footprint_wire.json and process_memory_wire.json fixture note: the platform holds byte-identical copies and fixture changes are coordinated with it.

Threat-model relevance:
- The removed console variables carried no secrets; the text warned against putting private credentials in NEXT_PUBLIC_* values. Removing the section drops a hygiene warning only from provider docs, since the console is out of scope per the threat model.
- The provider-owned sections that remain (add-on hold TB-012/T-059/T-060, App Attest worker, endpoint resumption/logout A-008/T-053, prefix cache T-041, GLM) are untouched in the visible head text and base ranges.
- Fixture-drift risk: the provider fixtures are mirrored in the platform. The new text asks for coordination but nothing enforces parity. This is a process matter, not a security regression.

I found no weakened controls, invalidated assumptions or new attack surface. I checked only the supplied excerpts. Patch excerpts for test.md and configuration.md are truncated, but the range maps are complete and head_text confirms the changed regions. I did not verify that the console-ui directory was actually removed elsewhere in the PR, so no cross-file claim is made.
